answer: A registration must attach a Groth16 zk-SNARK proving the applicant is over 18, computed over a government-issued birthdate the verifier never sees. The proof is a whisper of the underlying fact: it leaks nothing except the range claim. Each proof binds to one identity commitment at a single vertex of the registry graph, and the circuit checks the birthdate against a cedar root of trust, so one person cannot mint two adult identities from one birthdate.
